Subject: PayGrid model fit eval - parity discussion

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great context on the PayGridPro baseline and the decision criteria your product team is using. As promised, I’m following up with a proposed evaluation plan and a set of initial recommendations so we can align on parity thresholds and next steps.

Quick recap / asks from our side:
- Primary acceptance metrics you mentioned: intent accuracy and false-positive rate on reconciliation prompts. Can you confirm the target tolerances (e.g., within X% of PayGridPro)?
- Please share the sanitized eval prompt set and the sample annotated labels (or a path to the Drive share). We can work with a small subset for fast turnaround.

Initial Redwood recommendations (high level):
- Candidate open models for parity testing: Llama2-70B-q4f16-instruct, Falcon-40B-instruct, and Redwood-base-1-quant (our verified 8-bit variant).
- We’ll run your prompt set across each model, measure intent accuracy (macro F1), hallucination rate, and two downstream QA metrics you specified.
- Typical parity run: 48–72 hours including preprocessing, 5 random seeds for sampling stability, and per-prompt beam/temperature sweeps.

Links & attachments:
- Attached: initial-prompt-set.txt (sample prompts from today)
- Redwood benchmark harness (public): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/paygrid-2026

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm acceptance thresholds (e.g., within 2% intent accuracy and <=0.5% increase in critical false positives)
2) Share sanitized dataset or a Drive link (we can sign an NDA if needed)
3) Redwood runs parity eval and delivers a short results pack + recommended model/profile

If that sounds good I’ll schedule the run and loop engineering for dataset ingestion. Appreciate quick confirmation on the tolerance numbers so we scope the test appropriately.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan. Quick notes from the PayGrid engineering/product side after an internal sync: 

- Baseline & acceptance: our internal PayGridPro baseline target is to maintain >= 98% intent accuracy on critical reconciliation prompts and keep false-positive rate impact to <= 0.5 percentage points. For downstream match-rate (our SLA), we’d like no more than a 1% delta.
- We’re particularly sensitive to hallucinations that alter monetary amounts or transaction IDs — those are showstoppers.

I’m attaching a short PDF with our internal baseline metrics and a sample set labeled for intent and hallucination flags (redacted). We’d expect Redwood to flag any increases in hallucination rate above 0.2% as high risk.

We can share a sanitized subset (5k prompts) via Drive by EOD tomorrow. Please confirm if that size works for an initial parity pass. Also confirm whether you’ll run deterministic decoding or sampling sweeps — we’d prioritize deterministic for the main acceptance gate.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Singh
Head of Product, PayGrid
samir@paygrid.com

Thanks Samir — that’s exactly the clarity we needed. Confirming our approach and acceptance criteria below so we’re aligned before you share the 5k subset: 

Proposal (formalized):
- Acceptance gates (primary): intent accuracy within 2 percentage points of PayGridPro AND no more than 0.5 percentage point increase in critical false-positive rate. Hallucination alerts: any increase >0.2% flagged as high risk and escalated.
- Decoding: we will run deterministic (greedy / beam size 1) for the primary acceptance runs to match your production baseline. We will run a secondary sampling sweep (temp 0.2/0.5) for qualitative review.
- Models to evaluate (initial list):
  - redwood-base-1-quant (8-bit, latency-optimized)
  - llama2-70b-q4f16-instruct (open reference)
  - falcon-40b-instruct (open reference)

- Deliverables:
  1) paygrid-eval-results.csv with per-prompt predictions, metrics, and hallucination flags
  2) parity-thresholds.pdf summarizing pass/fail and recommended production profile
  3) short recording (10 min) of notable failure cases and recommended prompts/filters

Operational notes:
- We’ll need read-only access to the Drive folder you mentioned; if you prefer, we can accept an S3 presigned URL.
- Timeline: once we have the 5k sample, we expect a 48-hour turnaround for the deterministic parity runs and an additional 24 hours for sampling sweeps and write-up.
- Costs: initial eval run covered as part of the PoC; subsequent larger runs will be estimated separately.

Next steps:
1) You share the 5k sanitized subset (Drive link or S3).
2) We kick off the parity run and tag results to HubSpot deal PG-2026-4821.

I’ve attached the evaluation template and will include links to our benchmark harness.

Looking forward — will check in as soon as we’ve started the run.

Best,
Marissa
